text:
Hannah Lee: dropped a quick prototype for an inline micro-sampling control in the p95 header: https://redwood.design/mock/2172501111.png. goal: keep card height fixed, make density obvious without full slider. PTAL.

Tom Rivera: nice. question: how discoverable is the inline control? recommend a hover tooltip + small chevron to indicate expand.

Maya Patel: a11y note: make the chip a real button (44px hit target) with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. label should be "Sampling density". helper text: "% of requests used for latency aggregates. Higher = more accurate, higher cost."

Ethan Brooks: infra: avoid resampling on every hover/preview. plan: client-only preview while interacting, commit on close/apply with 600ms coalesce. add gateway metric `sampling.commit.rate` and throttle >5/s.

Tom Rivera: visual nit: animate chip value changes and crossfade heatmap buckets. freeze y-axis for 800ms while new data streams to avoid jitter.

Zoe (design-bot): accessibility checks: chip contrast 3.0:1 (fail). recommend darker text or lighter background to reach >=4.5:1. also add `aria-live="polite"` announcements when density changes.

Maya Patel: keyboard spec: Enter/Space opens inline panel, Arrow keys adjust 1%, Shift+Arrow 5%, Home/End min/max, Escape closes. Announce: "Sampling density set to X percent".

Hannah Lee: action items: Tom update mock with chevron + micro-animate, Maya finalize copy and keyboard spec, Ethan wire gateway coalesce + metric, I'll upload hi-fi with contrast update before Friday. leaving open for design sync. :sparkles:
